title: Particles, antiparticles and classification; Pair production and annihilation; Fundamental interactions and exchange particles; Conservation laws in particle interactions; Mass defect and binding energy; Fission and reactors; Fusion; Force on a current-carrying conductor

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Electromagnetic interaction
items.clue: Acts on charged particles only; infinite range.

items.label: Flavour
items.clue: Name for the type of a quark, such as up or down.

items.label: Weak interaction
items.clue: Acts on all quarks and all leptons; range about 10⁻¹⁸ m.

items.label: Meson
items.clue: Particle made of a quark and an antiquark, such as a pion.

questions.stem: A straight wire lies in the plane of the page and carries a current towards the right of the page. A uniform magnetic field in the plane of the page is directed towards the top of the page. What is the direction of the force on the wire?

options.text: Towards the top of the page
Towards the right of the page
Out of the plane of the page
Into the plane of the page

questions.stem: Radium-226 decays by α emission: ²²⁶₈₈Ra → ²²²₈₆Rn + ⁴₂α. The atomic masses are 226.025410 u for radium-226, 222.017578 u for radon-222 and 4.002603 u for helium-4 (the electron masses cancel). Take 1 u = 1.66 × 10⁻²⁷ kg = 931.5 MeV c⁻², 1 eV = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ J and c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. How much energy is released in the decay of one radium-226 nucleus?

Some very heavy nuclides, such as californium-252, can undergo spontaneous fission, whereas uranium-235 in a reactor undergoes neutron-induced fission. Which statement about spontaneous fission is correct?

options.text: Energy is released as kinetic energy of an α particle that breaks off the nucleus.
Energy is released only once the material is hot enough for its nuclei to shake apart.
No energy is released, as no neutron has been absorbed to supply the energy.
Energy is released when the nucleus splits into two fragments of comparable mass.

questions.stem: In the fusion reaction ²₁H + ³₁H → ⁴₂He + ¹₀n, the binding energies per nucleon are 1.11 MeV for ²₁H, 2.83 MeV for ³₁H and 7.07 MeV for ⁴₂He. A free neutron has no binding energy. How much energy is released in one reaction?
Two protons collide at high energy: p + p → p + n + X, where X stands for all the other particles produced. What must the total charge of X be?
questions.explanation: Before: +1 + 1 = +2e. After: +1 + 0 + X. Charge is conserved, so X = +1e (for example a positron with a neutrino, or a positive pion).

questions.stem: An electron and a positron annihilate, producing two photons. Which quantity is different after the annihilation from before it?
questions.explanation: Photons have no rest mass. The pair's mass has been converted to photon energy, but energy and momentum are conserved.

questions.stem: A straight wire 0.40 m long carries a current of 3.0 A. Only 0.25 m of the wire lies inside a uniform magnetic field of strength 0.080 T, and the wire makes an angle of 30° with the direction of the field. What is the magnitude of the force on the wire?
Predict first. Which statement correctly describes the binding energy of a nucleus?

options.text: The energy released when the nucleus is separated completely into its nucleons.
The energy stored inside the nucleus, which it gives out when it later decays.
The minimum energy needed to pull the nucleus apart into separate nucleons.
The energy equivalent of the extra mass a nucleus has over its separate nucleons.

questions.stem: A uranium-235 nucleus absorbs a neutron and splits into two fragments and 2 free neutrons. The fragments contain 234 nucleons in total. The binding energy per nucleon is 7.6 MeV for uranium-235 and about 8.5 MeV for the fragments. A free neutron has no binding energy. Roughly how much energy is released?
questions.explanation: Energy released = increase in total binding energy = 234 × 8.5 − 235 × 7.6 = 1989 − 1786 ≈ 200 MeV.

questions.stem: A student proposes that a free neutron decays into a proton and an electron and nothing else: n → p + e⁻. Which conservation law that holds in all nuclear decays would this proposal break?

options.text: Charge, since two charged particles would come from one neutral particle
Baryon number, since a neutron would be replaced by a proton
Lepton number, since the number of electrons and neutrinos would rise
Mass, since the proton and electron have less mass than the neutron

questions.stem: An electron and a positron, each with 0.30 MeV of kinetic energy, collide head-on and annihilate into two photons. The rest energy of an electron is 0.511 MeV. What is the energy of each photon?
questions.explanation: Head-on with equal energies, the total momentum is zero, so the two photons have equal energies and fly apart in opposite directions. Each: 0.511 + 0.30 = 0.81 MeV.

questions.stem: In a current-balance experiment, 5.0 cm of a horizontal wire lies at right angles to the field between the poles of a magnet resting on a balance. With no current the balance reads 152.46 g. With a current of 3.0 A it reads 152.10 g. Take g = 9.81 N kg⁻¹. What is the magnetic flux density between the poles?
